catalyst_summary: Titan holds 6.59% institutional allocation (tied #2 top holding) backed by a +3.00% active overweight on Retail Jewellery. The structural thesis is propelled by organized jewellery penetration expanding from 38% in FY24 to 43% in FY29 within an overall jewellery market expanding from $80B to $165B (12% CAGR). Long-term tailwinds stem from upper-middle and high-income households (>₹6L+) surging from 69M (24%) in 2018 to 197M (51%) by 2030, alongside custom duty rationalization curbing unorganized gray-market channels.

Maruti Suzuki represents 6.59% portfolio allocation (tied #2 holding) within an overall -5.91% active underweight on Auto OEMs. The structural PV market has decisively shifted towards SUVs (expanding to 56.0% of PV volume in FY25E from 18.3% in FY17), while entry-level hatchbacks collapsed to 23.5% (down from 50.0% in FY17). While Maruti's SUV offensive (Brezza, Grand Vitara, Fronx) defends volumes, the overall sector faces commodity price headwinds, moderating volume growth, and rich valuations.

Mahindra & Mahindra commands 6.51% conviction allocation (#4 holding), directly capturing the SUV megatrend where category penetration crossed 56% of Indian PVs. Discretionary demand is further augmented by macroeconomic catalysts including $10-$12B personal income tax relief (concentrated in ₹12L-₹50L salary brackets), 8th Pay Commission wage hikes effective Jan 2026 benefiting 10M+ mid-income households, and healthy rural cash flows supporting tractor volumes.

Trent commands 4.80% allocation (#6 holding) as the primary vehicle in the fund's largest active sector tilt (+10.27% Overweight on Retail). The institutional thesis rides organized apparel penetration rising from 50% in FY24 to 57% in FY29 in a $116B apparel TAM. Trent's Zudio format leads fast-fashion store expansion, leveraging nuclear family shopping behavior and social media-driven Gen-Z aspirational consumption.

catalyst_summary: ITC holds 4.40% allocation (#7 holding) amid sector underweights on Tobacco (-4.36%) and FMCG (-4.85%). With FMCG sector EBITDA margins plateauing at 23% in FY24 (after rising from 15% in FY11), future earnings rely strictly on volume growth and premiumization rather than margin expansion.

Building material sequencing models place decorative paint demand concentrated in Year 4 and Completion stages, providing volume support against heightened industry competitive intensity.

The brand benefits from aspirational leisure travel, upper-middle household wealth expansion, and growing export volumes.

VBL continues to outgrow the broader staples universe through chilling infrastructure expansion, Sting energy drink hyper-growth, and expanding distribution footprint into under-penetrated rural territories.

semantic_text: Eternal Limited (erstwhile Zomato Limited) stands as the #1 institutional conviction holding in the fund at 6.89% allocation. Eternal operates a multi-pronged consumer internet ecosystem encompassing Zomato food delivery (operating in a ₹600B GOV sector expanding at 57% CAGR, with Indian online food penetration at just 8% vs 53% in China), Blinkit quick commerce (commanding ~13% share of online grocery via a rapid dark-store rollout), Hyperpure B2B restaurant supply, and the District going-out entertainment platform. Supported by Gen-Z / millennial aspirational convenience and nuclear family formation, Eternal is achieving strong operating leverage as platform fees, advertising revenues, and dark store densities drive expanding consolidated EBITDA margins.

semantic_text: Bharti Airtel represents the fund's #5 conviction holding at 6.29% allocation. Operating as the premier quality subscriber anchor in India's consolidated telecom duopoly alongside Reliance Jio, Airtel serves as the essential digital pipe powering India's expansion towards 1+ billion internet users by 2030 (67%–69% penetration). The investment thesis is anchored in sustained tariff repair driving blended ARPU from ₹200+ toward ₹300+, 5G network monetization as per-capita data consumption escalates, high-margin postpaid churn defense, Airtel Xstream home fiber expansion, and Nxtra enterprise hyperscale data centers capitalizing on national AI and cloud hosting demand.
